Here’s a quick‑reference guide to the most effective leg exercises—grouped by type, with key form notes, typical rep ranges, and equipment options. Pick a mix that fits your goals (strength, hypertrophy, endurance, or functional fitness) and your current level. | # | Exercise | Primary Muscles | Equipment | Typical Sets × Reps | Key Form Tips | |---|----------|-----------------|-----------|---------------------|---------------| | 1 | **Back Squat** | Quadriceps, glutes, hamstrings, core | Barbell, squat rack | 3–5 × 4–8 | • Feet ~ shoulder width, toes slightly out.
• Keep chest up, spine neutral.
• Descend until thighs ≥ parallel.
• Drive through heels. | | 2 | **Front Squat** | Quads, core, upper back | Barbell, squat rack | 3–5 × 4–8 | • Bar on front delts, elbows high.
• Keep torso upright.
• Same depth as back squat. | | 3 | **Goblet Squat** | Quads, glutes, core | Dumbbell or kettlebell | 3–4 × 8–12 | • Hold weight at chest.
• Keep elbows inside knees.
• Depth to parallel or deeper. | | 4 | **Bulgarian Split Squat** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Bench or box, dumbbells | 3–4 × 6–10 per leg | • Rear foot elevated on bench.
• Front knee tracks over toes.
• Keep torso upright. | | 5 | **Walking Lunge** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Bodyweight or dumbbells | 3–4 × 10–15 per leg | • Long stride, knee over ankle.
• Keep chest forward.
• Alternate legs. | | 6 | **Romanian Deadlift** | Hamstrings, glutes, lower back | Barbell or dumbbells | 3–4 × 6–10 | • Slight knee bend, hips hinge.
• Keep bar close to shins.
• Neutral spine. | | 7 | **Sumo Deadlift** | Inner thighs, glutes, hamstrings | Barbell | 3–4 × 4–8 | • Wide stance, toes out.
• Pull through hips, not shoulders.
• Keep chest up. | | 8 | **Hip Thrust / Glute Bridge** | Glutes, hamstrings | Barbell or bodyweight | 3–4 × 8–12 | • Upper back on bench.
• Drive through heels, squeeze glutes at top.
• Avoid hyperextension. | | 9 | **Leg Press** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Leg press machine | 3–4 × 8–12 | • Foot placement ~ mid‑calf.
• Full range, avoid locking knees.
• Control eccentric phase. | | 10 | **Calf Raise (Standing or Seated)** | Gastrocnemius, soleus | Bodyweight, dumbbells, calf raise machine | 3–4 × 12–20 | • Full stretch at bottom, full contraction at top.
• Slow controlled movement. | | 11 | **Step‑Up** | Quads, glutes | Bench or box, dumbbells | 3–4 × 8–12 per leg | • Drive through heel of stepping leg.
• Keep knee tracking over toes.
• Use a stable platform. | | 12 | **Box Jump / Plyo Jump** | Quads, glutes, calves, core | Plyo box | 3–4 × 6–8 | • Soft landing, knees slightly bent.
• Use arms for momentum.
• Focus on explosive power. | --- ### How to Build a Balanced Leg Routine | Goal | Sample Weekly Plan | Notes | |------|--------------------|-------| | **Strength (Power)** | **Day 1**: Back Squat 5×5, Romanian Deadlift 4×5, Walking Lunge 3×8 per leg
**Day 2**: Front Squat 5×5, Hip Thrust 4×6, Calf Raise 4×12 | Heavy loads, low reps. Rest 2–3 min between sets. | | **Hypertrophy (Muscle Growth)** | **Day 1**: Back Squat 4×8, Bulgarian Split Squat 3×10, Leg Press 3×12
**Day 2**: Romanian Deadlift 4×8, Hip Thrust 3×12, Calf Raise 4×15 | Moderate loads, 60–90 s rest. | | **Endurance / Conditioning** | **Day 1**: Goblet Squat 3×15, Walking Lunge 3×20, Step‑Up 3×15 per leg
**Day 2**: Bodyweight Squat 3×30, Calf Raise 3×25, Box Jump 3×10 | Light loads, short rest (30–45 s). | | **Functional / Mobility** | **Day 1**: Hip Thrust 3×10, Walking Lunge 3×12, Calf Raise 3×12
**Day 2**: Goblet Squat 3×12, Step‑Up 3×12, Bodyweight Squat 3×20 | Focus on joint health, use foam roller after. | *If you’re new, start with 2–3 leg sessions per week, gradually adding volume.* --- ### Common Mistakes & How to Fix Them | Mistake | Fix | |---------|-----| | **Knees caving inward** | Engage glutes, keep knees tracking over toes. | | **Rising hips too high** | Focus on driving through heels, keep torso upright. | | **Barbell too far forward** | Keep bar close to shins, avoid “swinging” the bar. | | **Not enough depth** | Aim for thighs ≥ parallel; use a lighter load if needed. | | **Neglecting calves** | Include calf raises; use both standing and seated variations. | --- ### Quick Warm‑Up (5–10 min) 1. **Dynamic leg swings** – front‑to‑back and side‑to‑side (30 s each). 2. **Bodyweight squats** – 2×10, focusing on depth. 3. **Hip circles** – 30 s each direction. 4. **Ankle mobility drills** – dorsiflexion/plantarflexion (30 s each). --- ### Cool‑Down & Recovery - **Static stretches**: quad stretch, hamstring stretch, calf stretch, hip flexor stretch (hold 30 s each). - **Foam rolling**: quads, hamstrings, IT band, calves (1–2 min each). - **Hydration & protein**: aim for 0.25–0.3 g protein per kg bodyweight within 30 min post‑workout. --- ### Final Tips - **Progressive overload**: add 2.5–5 kg or 1–2 reps every 1–2 weeks. - **Listen to your body**: if you feel sharp pain (not just soreness), stop and reassess form or load. - **Core stability matters**: a strong core protects your lower back during heavy lifts. - **Variation keeps it interesting**: swap in front squats, hack squats, or single‑leg presses every 4–6 weeks. Feel free to mix and match based on what feels best for you and your schedule. Happy training!
